answer: Kinsale does not disclose a combined ratio for the Commercial Property division. The company has one reportable segment (Excess and Surplus Lines Insurance) and reports loss, expense and combined ratios only on a consolidated basis: FY2025 combined ratio 75.9% (loss ratio 55.1%, expense ratio 20.8%) [H15-E1][H15-E2]. By division it discloses gross written premiums only; Commercial Property GWP was USD 374.5 million in 2025 (18.9% of total, down 17.9% from USD 456.2 million) [H15-E1]. A text search of the FY2025 10-K, the 2026 Q1/Q2 10-Qs, the Q4 2025 and 2026 Q1/Q2 earnings releases and the January 8, 2026 Investor Day slide text finds no combined or loss ratio tied to a named division [H15-E1][H15-E3][H15-E4].

output.answer:
## Answer

**Kinsale Capital Group does not publicly report a combined ratio for its Commercial Property division specifically — so there is no official 2025 figure for that division.**

Here's what the company actually discloses:

**Division-level reporting is limited to premiums, not profitability**
Kinsale has **one reportable segment** (its Excess & Surplus Lines Insurance segment) and reports loss/expense/combined ratios only at the consolidated company level. For individual underwriting divisions, it discloses only **gross written premiums** — not loss ratios or combined ratios.

- Commercial Property gross written premiums (2025): **$374.5 million**, down **17.9%** from $456.2 million in 2024 (driven by rate declines and heightened competition, including from standard carriers)
- Commercial Property = **18.9%** of 2025 gross written premiums (and ~11.1% of *net* written premiums), still the largest single division
- Source: [Kinsale 2025 10-K (SEC)](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1669162/000166916226000015/knsl-20251231.htm)

**Consolidated (company-wide) 2025 ratios**
- Combined ratio: **75.9%** (loss ratio 55.1% + expense ratio 20.8%)
- Q4 2025 combined ratio: 71.7%
- 2024 combined ratio: 76.4%
- Sources: [Kinsale Q4/FY2025 earnings release](https://ir.kinsalecapitalgroup.com/news/news-details/2026/Kinsale-Capital-Group-Inc--Reports-2025-Fourth-Quarter-and-Year-End-Results/default.aspx), [Kinsale IR overview](https://ir.kinsalecapitalgroup.com/overview/default.aspx)

**Why the gap matters:** Any "Commercial Property division combined ratio" you might see cited would be an analyst estimate or third-party calculation, not a Kinsale-reported figure. The company discusses property results indirectly — e.g., noting that favorable prior-year reserve development in 2025 was concentrated "primarily within property lines of business," and that catastrophe losses (largely the Palisades Fire) hit the 2025 loss ratio.

If you need a division-level combined ratio, it would have to be estimated from statutory filings (e.g., NAIC Annual Statement Schedule P / state-level data) rather than from Kinsale's SEC or investor disclosures.

Would you like me to try digging into statutory filings or analyst estimates for a derived Commercial Property figure?
